relations: Head rotation and tilting dislodge clinging droplets, propelling them outward into the surrounding air.
Rapid wing flapping blurs the appendages into streaks extending horizontally from the body.
The bird remains anchored to the twig while the head and wings execute continuous motion.
Detached droplets follow ballistic trajectories, drifting downward and away from the shaking bird.
caption: The video captures a high-speed close-up of a male hummingbird perched on a thin horizontal twig against a pure black background, its magenta-red gorget and head beaded with clinging water droplets. The bird remains perched on the twig while its head continuously rotates and tilts, the dark beak sweeping through a range of angles in an ongoing shaking motion already in progress. Some droplets cling to the crown and face and shift with the turning head, while others move away from it through the air. Its wings remain spread to either side, rendered as motion-blurred streaks. A free droplet at the lower edge of the breast drifts downward and leftward, separating from the bird. Numerous other droplets are airborne around it, changing position noticeably across the slow-motion views.
